verdict.reasoning: Patient states wheezing started about two days ago and that it 'gets a bit worse at night' ('it started, like, about two days ago' and 'it gets a bit worse at night').
Patient links onset to cleaning with dust exposure: 'I was, like, cleaning the house and, like, all this dust came out of the carpet... don't know if it was triggered by, you know...'.
Patient reports being 'a little bit short of breath' and 'sometimes I'm unable to complete my sentences'.
Patient denies pain with breathing ('No, no. No pain.') and denies dizziness ('No, no dizziness? None of that.').
When asked about eating and drinking, patient replies 'Yeah, yeah, I think I'm having, like, you know, four or five glasses a day', indicating intake is adequate.
Patient reports 'I used to have, like, a bit of asthma as a child'.
Patient says 'also in the summer, I sometimes get hay fever'.

Patient notes exertion-related symptoms and having an inhaler: 'sometimes when I run for, like, long periods, it can start up a bit, but I have, like, an asthma inhaler,' implying occasional use with exertion.
Doctor asks 'But you don't see your doctor regularly for asthma?' and patient replies 'No, I don't.'
Doctor asks 'when you get hay fever, do you take medications for it?' and patient responds 'Not really,' indicating no regular hay fever medications.
When advised to take an antihistamine if available, patient says 'Yeah, I don't have any antihistamines at home.'
Patient states 'I have before taken steroids for asthma.'
Transcript only addresses general allergies: 'Apart from this, do you know if you're allergic to anything?' Patient: 'Not that I know of.' No mention of drug allergies specifically.
When asked distance from a doctor's surgery, patient replies 'Maybe minutes drive away,' indicating a short driving distance.

Doctor frames it as asthma vs allergy related to dust: 'this could be one of two things, but we want to rule out asthma or an allergy first' and mentions 'in case it is an allergy you've had from the dust,' in the context of wheeze and shortness of breath.
Doctor explicitly references both: 'given that you've had a history of asthma when you were a child and you get hay fever sometimes in the summer'.
Doctor advises in-person assessment: 'what you need is visit one of our clinics so we can do some more tests' and later 'You can take yourself to the gp.'
Doctor states: 'we would do is use a small device on your finger to check the amount of oxygen in your blood,' describing pulse oximetry.

Doctor advises antihistamine before/around visit: 'if you've got something like an antihistamine... I would take one' and 'you might be able to get one on your way to the doctor's surgery. If not, they can prescribe you one.'
Doctor notes steroids may be needed after evaluation: 'you may need to take some steroids now. But we cannot... know until we've done those tests first.'
Doctor says: 'I'm going to write a letter for your GP just to let him know what's happened.'
